sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross-Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 你好，我是安德鲁·罗斯-索尔金。

sentences.en: I cover business and policy for Dealbook, a daily newsletter at the
sentences.zh: 我为《纽约时报》旗下的每日新闻简报《Dealbook》报道商业和政策新闻。

sentences.en: New York Times.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》。

sentences.en: On November 18th, I'm going to be interviewing some of the most consequential leaders in business, politics, and culture, including J.D.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我将在纽约市举行的Dealbook峰会上现场采访一些商业、政治和文化领域最有影响力的人物，包括J.D.

sentences.en: Vance, Elon Musk, Christine
sentences.zh: 万斯、埃隆·马斯克、克里斯蒂娜·

sentences.en: Lagarde, Zylran Mondani, and many others, live on stage at the Dealbook Summit in New York City.
sentences.zh: 拉加德、齐尔兰·蒙达尼以及其他许多嘉宾。

sentences.en: You can watch some of these unguarded, unfiltered conversations as they happen.
sentences.zh: 你可以观看其中一些毫无防备、未经剪辑的对话实况。

sentences.en: We're going to be live-streaming select interviews for anyone to watch, free, at nytimes.com on November 18th.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我们将在nytimes.com上直播部分采访，供所有人免费观看。

sentences.en: If you're not already a subscriber, you can download the New York Times app to watch and get a month of free access to all of our journalism.
sentences.zh: 如果你还不是订阅用户，可以下载《纽约时报》App进行观看，并获得我们所有新闻报道的一个月免费访问权限。

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 希望你能收看。

sentences.en: You won't want to miss it.
sentences.zh: 你一定不想错过。

sentences.en: From the New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》的迈克尔·巴尔巴罗。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《每日新闻》节目。

sentences.en: Today.
sentences.zh: 今日话题。

sentences.en: The operation went undetected for months, giving foreign agents access to the inner workings of American government.
sentences.zh: 这次行动在数月内未被察觉，使外国特工得以接触到美国政府的核心运作。

sentences.en: My colleague, David Sanger, on who was behind the attack and why it keeps happening to the U.S.
sentences.zh: 我的同事大卫·桑格将讲述谁是这次袭击的幕后黑手，以及为什么这种事总是在美国身上发生。

sentences.en: It's Wednesday, December 16th.
sentences.zh: 今天是12月16日，星期三。

sentences.en: U.S.
sentences.zh: 美国

sentences.en: officials believe Russia is behind a massive cyber attack targeting the U.S.
sentences.zh: 官员认为，俄罗斯是一次针对美国

sentences.en: Treasury and Commerce Department.
sentences.zh: 财政部和商务部的大规模网络攻击的幕后黑手。

sentences.en: Sources say it may be one of the biggest and most sophisticated hacks in years, and it may have been launched in the spring.
sentences.zh: 消息人士称，这可能是近年来规模最大、最复杂的黑客攻击之一，且可能早在春季就已经发动。

sentences.en: Hackers appear to have accessed sensitive information as far back as March.
sentences.zh: 黑客似乎早在三月份就已经获取了敏感信息。

sentences.en: U.S.
sentences.zh: 美国

sentences.en: officials are scrambling to try to figure out what data was taken, what other departments may have been breached.
sentences.zh: 官员们正忙于查明哪些数据被窃取，以及还有哪些部门可能遭到了入侵。

sentences.en: The actors behind this campaign gained access to numerous public and private organizations around the world.
sentences.zh: 此次行动的幕后黑手渗透了全球众多公共和私营机构。

sentences.en: One government official telling Reuters, quote, this is a much bigger story than one single agency.
sentences.zh: 一位政府官员告诉路透社，引用原话：“这不仅仅是一个机构的问题，故事远比这大得多。”

sentences.en: This is a huge cyber espionage campaign targeting the U.S.
sentences.zh: 这是一场针对美国

sentences.en: government and its interests.
sentences.zh: 政府及其利益的巨大网络间谍活动。

sentences.en: David, tell me about this attack.
sentences.zh: 大卫，跟我说说这次袭击。

sentences.en: Well, Michael, we're still learning a lot, and there's a lot we have to say we don't really know yet.
sentences.zh: 嗯，迈克尔，我们还在了解很多情况，而且有很多事情我们不得不承认目前还不清楚。

sentences.en: But here's what we have pieced together.
sentences.zh: 但这是我们目前拼凑出的情况。

sentences.en: Sometime around March, a very sophisticated group of hackers who clearly worked for a nation state,
sentences.zh: 大约在三月份，一个显然为国家效力的、非常老练的黑客组织，

sentences.en: we believe Russian intelligence, broke into the computer systems of a range of U.S.
sentences.zh: 我们认为是俄罗斯情报部门，闯入了美国一系列

sentences.en: government agencies, the Treasury, the Commerce Department, the Los Alamos National Laboratory, which makes nuclear weapons and designs them, the State Department.
sentences.zh: 政府机构的计算机系统，包括财政部、商务部、负责制造和设计核武器的洛斯阿拉莫斯国家实验室，以及国务院。

sentences.en: But at the time, no one saw any of this.
sentences.zh: 但在当时，没有人发现这一切。

sentences.en: And so as we've been able to go reconstruct it in recent days, it looks like one of the reasons we missed it was that it was an incredibly sophisticated approach
sentences.zh: 所以正如我们最近几天能够还原的那样，我们之所以错过它，原因之一是这是一种极其复杂的方法，

sentences.en: in which the hackers didn't go right after those different institutions, didn't try to get directly into their networks.
sentences.zh: 黑客并没有直接针对那些不同的机构，也没有试图直接进入它们的网络。

sentences.en: But instead, they got into a kind of software that government agencies,
sentences.zh: 相反，他们进入了一种政府机构、

sentences.en: Fortune 500 companies, the New York Times, all use.
sentences.zh: 《财富》500强企业、《纽约时报》都在使用的软件。

sentences.en: It is software made by a company called SolarWinds in Texas.
sentences.zh: 这是一款由德克萨斯州一家名为SolarWinds的公司制造的软件。

sentences.en: Most consumers have never heard of them.
sentences.zh: 大多数消费者从未听说过他们。

sentences.en: I had barely heard of them until a few days ago.
sentences.zh: 直到几天前，我也几乎没听说过他们。

sentences.en: And what they make is network monitoring software.
sentences.zh: 他们制造的是网络监控软件。

sentences.en: So it's a real sort of backroom engineering thing.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一种非常幕后的工程技术产品。

sentences.en: But the brilliance of attacking through this software is that you're essentially getting into the supply chain that feeds the rest of the U.S.
sentences.zh: 但通过这种软件进行攻击的精妙之处在于，你本质上是进入了供应美国

sentences.en: government and corporate America.
sentences.zh: 政府和美国企业界的供应链。

sentences.en: And so you don't need to break into companies or agencies.
sentences.zh: 所以你不需要去闯入那些公司或机构。

sentences.en: If you can get into this software, it will take you into the government agencies.
sentences.zh: 只要你能进入这个软件，它就会带你进入政府机构。

sentences.en: What do you mean?
sentences.zh: 你是什么意思？

sentences.en: So imagine, Michael, that this wasn't a cyber attack, but it was in the physical world.
sentences.zh: 想象一下，迈克尔，如果这不是网络攻击，而是在现实世界中。

sentences.en: And you were trying to take out a bunch of tanks that were being produced for the Army.
sentences.zh: 你试图摧毁一批为军队生产的坦克。

sentences.en: One way to do it would be to try to creep into the tank factory and, you know, sabotage the parts.
sentences.zh: 一种方法是潜入坦克工厂，你知道的，破坏零件。

sentences.en: But you might get caught.
sentences.zh: 但你可能会被抓住。

sentences.en: And if you got caught, you'd probably either get shot or arrested.
sentences.zh: 如果你被抓住了，你可能会被枪毙或逮捕。

sentences.en: Wouldn't it be easier to get into the much smaller company that feeds ball bearings to the tanks
sentences.zh: 如果进入那家为坦克提供滚珠轴承的小得多的公司，

sentences.en: and make sure that all those ball bearings were flattened on one side.
sentences.zh: 并确保所有那些滚珠轴承的一侧都被压扁，岂不是更容易？

sentences.en: So you've been a lot more effective and you've taken a lot less risk.
sentences.zh: 这样你不仅效率高得多，而且承担的风险也小得多。

sentences.en: So these hackers got into the ball bearings of these government agencies' online presence.
sentences.zh: 所以这些黑客进入了这些政府机构在线办公系统的“滚珠轴承”。

sentences.en: They got into SolarWinds, the ball bearing in the metaphor, and they screwed that up.
sentences.zh: 他们进入了SolarWinds，也就是这个比喻中的滚珠轴承，并搞砸了它。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So once they got into this SolarWinds network monitoring software that nobody usually pays
sentences.zh: 所以一旦他们进入了这种通常没人注意的SolarWinds网络监控软件，

sentences.en: attention to, except if you're an IT engineer sitting in the back room, then they suddenly had tremendous access throughout the system.
sentences.zh: 除非你是坐在后台的IT工程师，否则他们突然就在整个系统中拥有了巨大的访问权限。

sentences.en: And if they were careful about it, they could keep that access without getting caught.
sentences.zh: 如果他们小心谨慎，就能在不被发现的情况下保持这种访问权限。

sentences.en: David, why are we convinced that this was Russian hackers?
sentences.zh: 大卫，为什么我们确信这是俄罗斯黑客干的？

sentences.en: Did they leave behind any evidence that allows us to say, ah, those are the marks of Russia?
sentences.zh: 他们留下了什么证据让我们能说，啊，这就是俄罗斯的标记吗？

sentences.en: Well, a few things.
sentences.zh: 嗯，有几点。

sentences.en: First, the skill level.
sentences.zh: 首先是技术水平。

sentences.en: This was done with a precision and with an understanding of the systems that 97% of the world's best hackers wouldn't have the time or the resources to pull off.
sentences.zh: 这是以一种精准度完成的，并且对系统的理解程度，是世界上97%的顶尖黑客都没有时间和资源去实现的。

sentences.en: The second thing is they use certain techniques that have been seen before by the Russians.
sentences.zh: 第二点是他们使用了某些俄罗斯人以前使用过的技术。

sentences.en: It had the markings not just of the Russians, but of a particular intelligence agency within
sentences.zh: 这不仅有俄罗斯人的特征，而且有俄罗斯内部一个特定情报机构的特征，

sentences.en: Russia called the SVR.
sentences.zh: 叫做对外情报局（SVR）。

sentences.en: This is the group, a successor to the old KGB from Soviet days, that is out there mostly for espionage purposes.
sentences.zh: 这是苏联时期老克格勃的继任者，主要从事间谍活动。

sentences.en: That said, it's entirely conceivable that a few months from now we could come to a conclusion that the early findings were wrong.
sentences.zh: 话虽如此，完全有可能在几个月后，我们得出结论说早期的调查结果是错误的。

sentences.en: But nobody that I've spoken to in both the government or in the private sector seems to have a whole lot of doubt here.
sentences.zh: 但我在政府和私营部门交谈过的任何人，似乎对此都没有太多怀疑。

sentences.en: So what did these presumed Russian hackers actually take or look at?
sentences.zh: 那么这些被推测为俄罗斯的黑客到底窃取或查看了什么？

sentences.en: What do we know at this point?
sentences.zh: 目前我们知道些什么？

sentences.en: So, Michael, that's what everyone wants to know.
sentences.zh: 迈克尔，这正是每个人都想知道的。

sentences.en: And it's the biggest mystery right now.
sentences.zh: 这也是目前最大的谜团。

sentences.en: We do know that the Russians were into the email systems at the Treasury Department in
sentences.zh: 我们确实知道俄罗斯人进入了财政部的电子邮件系统，以及

sentences.en: one particular agency of the Commerce Department that deals with technology and internet issues.
sentences.zh: 商务部一个专门处理技术和互联网问题的特定机构。

sentences.en: We know that they were into the State Department, where in the past they have broken in before
sentences.zh: 我们知道他们进入了国务院，他们过去曾入侵过那里，

sentences.en: and have obviously interest in both diplomatic communications, but also trying to find diplomats who may be undercover as spies.
sentences.zh: 显然对外交通讯感兴趣，同时也试图寻找可能伪装成间谍的外交官。

sentences.en: We know that they were inside the Los Alamos nuclear laboratory, and their interest there is clear.
sentences.zh: 我们知道他们进入了洛斯阿拉莫斯核实验室，他们在那里的意图很明确。

sentences.en: That's the place where we design new nuclear weapons, think about cyber issues and encryption issues and so forth.
sentences.zh: 那是我们设计新型核武器、思考网络问题和加密问题等的地方。

sentences.en: So this sounds like classic espionage, and it sounds like a pretty bad case of it.
sentences.zh: 听起来这像是典型的间谍活动，而且是一个相当糟糕的案例。

sentences.en: If you're in the United States, Russia rooting around in highly sensitive corners of agencies and getting the kind of information that any government zealously seeks to protect.
sentences.zh: 如果你身处美国，俄罗斯在政府机构高度敏感的角落里翻找，获取任何政府都极力保护的信息。

sentences.en: That's absolutely right.
sentences.zh: 绝对正确。

sentences.en: And let's face it, this is highly embarrassing for the world's greatest cyber superpower, right?
sentences.zh: 而且让我们面对现实吧，这对世界头号网络超级大国来说是非常尴尬的，对吧？

sentences.en: And so I can imagine that the Trump administration, in its last five weeks in office, isn't especially
sentences.zh: 所以我可以想象，特朗普政府在任期的最后五周里，并不特别

sentences.en: interested in admitting that under their watch, whole departments of government got cleaned out.
sentences.zh: 愿意承认在他们的眼皮底下，整个政府部门都被洗劫一空了。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: David, at the beginning of our conversation, you said this attack had begun in March, but we have only just seemed to learn about it a couple of weeks ago, which, if I'm doing
sentences.zh: 大卫，在谈话开始时，你说这次袭击始于三月份，但我们似乎直到几周前才得知，如果我

sentences.en: my math correctly, suggests that Russian hackers have been rooting around in our government systems for like eight or nine months, which is a really long time.
sentences.zh: 没算错的话，这表明俄罗斯黑客已经在我们的政府系统中潜伏了八九个月，这可是很长一段时间。

sentences.en: So why did it take so long?
sentences.zh: 那么为什么花了这么长时间？

sentences.en: Well, that's a really great question, Michael.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这是一个非常好的问题，迈克尔。

sentences.en: And part of the answer, I think, is a technical one, that the US government has basically set
sentences.zh: 我认为部分答案是技术性的，美国政府基本上在自己的网络中设置了

sentences.en: up sensors throughout its own networks, looking for hackers coming in or trying to steal passwords and so forth.
sentences.zh: 传感器，用来寻找入侵的黑客或试图窃取密码的行为等等。

sentences.en: But none of that got set off here.
sentences.zh: 但这里并没有触发任何警报。

sentences.en: And the reason for that is they had gotten into this software that was legitimately considered a part of the US systeMs.
sentences.zh: 原因在于他们进入了这种被合法视为美国系统一部分的软件。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And then there may be one other thing, Michael.
sentences.zh: 而且可能还有另一件事，迈克尔。

sentences.en: It could have been the distraction of the election.
sentences.zh: 可能是因为大选的分心。

sentences.en: What do you mean?
sentences.zh: 什么意思？

sentences.en: Well, for the past year, the National Security Agency, General Paul Nakasone, who also runs
sentences.zh: 嗯，在过去的一年里，国家安全局局长保罗·中曾根（General Paul Nakasone），他同时也负责

sentences.en: United States Cyber Command, has said his number one responsibility was to protect this election against foreign attackers.
sentences.zh: 美国网络司令部，曾表示他的首要职责是保护这次选举免受外国攻击者的侵害。

sentences.en: And so he was looking for attacks on the election networks, on the registration systems, on voting machines, on the way we tally.
sentences.zh: 所以他一直在寻找针对选举网络、登记系统、投票机以及计票方式的攻击。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: A legitimate thing to do, given what's happened in recent times.
sentences.zh: 考虑到最近发生的事情，这是一件合情合理的事情。

sentences.en: So they were all looking over here.
sentences.zh: 所以他们都在盯着这边。

sentences.en: And maybe the Russians, who understood exactly what we were doing, thought this would be a great opportunity to go rob the bank while the police are down the street trying to stop
sentences.zh: 也许俄罗斯人，他们完全了解我们在做什么，认为当警察在街头试图阻止

sentences.en: a riot.
sentences.zh: 骚乱时，这正是去抢劫银行的大好机会。

sentences.en: But on a more serious note, look, there's a reason that I call this the perfect weapon.
sentences.zh: 但说得严肃一点，看，我称之为“完美武器”是有原因的。

sentences.en: It's dirt cheap.
sentences.zh: 它极其廉价。

sentences.en: It's virtually invisible.
sentences.zh: 它几乎隐形。

sentences.en: It lends itself to highly skilled engineers who could be working half a world away and don't have to physically enter your territory.
sentences.zh: 它非常适合那些远在半个地球之外、无需亲自进入你领土的高技能工程师。

sentences.en: It's what makes cyber attacks so hard to defend againSt.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么网络攻击如此难以防御的原因。

sentences.en: And it's the reason that cyber has become the primary way, the primary way that countries seek to undercut each other's power in various forMs.
sentences.zh: 这也是为什么网络攻击已成为各国在各种形式上试图削弱对方力量的主要手段。

sentences.en: And for the Russians, you know, they've been doing this for a quarter century.
sentences.zh: 对于俄罗斯人来说，你知道，他们已经这样做四分之一个世纪了。

sentences.en: There's a long history of this.
sentences.zh: 这有着悠久的历史。

sentences.en: It's just that they're getting better and better and better.
sentences.zh: 只是他们变得越来越强了。

sentences.en: And if there's one lesson from all this, Michael, it's that American defenses, that is both
sentences.zh: 如果说这一切有一个教训，迈克尔，那就是美国的防御，也就是

sentences.en: the ability to deter attacks from happening and deal with them when they do, has not been anywhere near as effective as it needs to be.
sentences.zh: 威慑攻击发生的能力以及在攻击发生时应对的能力，远未达到应有的有效水平。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: The New York Times app, unlocked.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》App，解锁全部内容。

sentences.en: Everyone knows you need to subscribe to The Times to access all of the reporting.
sentences.zh: 每个人都知道你需要订阅《时报》才能访问所有的报道。

sentences.en: But what if you could explore The Times for a month, for free, without putting in a credit card?
sentences.zh: 但如果能免费试用《时报》一个月，且无需输入信用卡信息呢？

sentences.en: Now you can.
sentences.zh: 现在你可以了。

sentences.en: When you download The New York Times app for the first time, your first month in the app is free.
sentences.zh: 当你第一次下载《纽约时报》App时，你在App里的第一个月是免费的。

sentences.en: A month to go behind the paywall to see what Times subscribers get every single day.
sentences.zh: 用一个月的时间越过付费墙，看看《时报》订阅者每天都能获得什么。

sentences.en: If you don't already subscribe to The New York Times, download The Times app today and get free access for 30 days.
sentences.zh: 如果你还没有订阅《纽约时报》，今天就下载《时报》App，获得30天的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: David, you just started to hint at this.
sentences.zh: 大卫，你刚才开始暗示这一点。

sentences.en: But where does this presumed Russian cyber attack fit into the history of Russian cyber attacks against the United States?
sentences.zh: 但这次被推测为俄罗斯的网络攻击在俄罗斯针对美国的网络攻击史上处于什么位置？

sentences.en: Well, there's a long history here, Michael.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这里有一段很长的历史，迈克尔。

sentences.en: But, you know, it really starts in the mid-1990s when there was an attack called Moonlight
sentences.zh: 但你知道，它确实始于90年代中期，当时发生了一次名为“月光迷宫”的攻击，

sentences.en: Maze, in which the Russians got into the Colorado School of Mines because they figured out it was connected to a whole bunch of military bases.

sentences.en: Because if there's anybody who might have a strong rationale for taking a very hard line against Russia, you might think that it would be Joe Biden.
sentences.zh: 他们偏向唐纳德·特朗普。

sentences.en: And I say that because we know from lots of reporting that the Russians did not want Joe Biden to win.
sentences.zh: 那么，我们的候任总统在应对像刚刚发生的这类攻击时，是否可能采取比前任强硬得多的态度？

sentences.en: They favored Donald Trump.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他会尝试，但这将是一个非常难以把握的平衡。

sentences.en: And so is it possible that our incoming president might take a much stronger approach than his predecessors when it comes to responding to things like this attack that just occurred?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他的优势在于他绝不亏欠普京任何东西，对吧？

sentences.en: Well, he's going to try, but it's going to be a really hard needle to thread.
sentences.zh: 他已经说过，普京不希望我当总统。

sentences.en: I mean, what he's got going for him is that he's not beholden to Putin in any way, right?
sentences.zh: 普京在针对我，如果他这么做，我也会反击他。

sentences.en: He's already said, Putin doesn't want me to be president.
sentences.zh: 他对此表达得相当明确。

sentences.en: Putin's coming after me, and if he does, I'm coming after him.
sentences.zh: 但说你要反击他，和真正做到这一点，将是一件困难的事情。

sentences.en: And he's been pretty explicit about that.
sentences.zh: 因为过去25年的历史表明，出于各种正当理由，我们迄今为止一直不愿与核大国进行充分的升级对抗。

sentences.en: But to say that you're coming after him and to actually do it is going to be a difficult thing.
sentences.zh: 而他明白这一点。

sentences.en: Because the history of these past 25 years, since Midnight Mays, is that we have so far been unwilling to escalate enough with the nuclear power for all kinds of good reasons.
sentences.zh: 所以拜登面临的问题是，他能否找到一种方法来把握这个平衡？

sentences.en: And he understands this.
sentences.zh: 他是否会加速中曾根将军的战略？

sentences.en: So the question for Biden is, is he going to find a way to thread the needle?
sentences.zh: 他是否能找到方法建立那些更好的防御系统？

sentences.en: Is he going to go accelerate General Nakasone's strategy?
sentences.zh: 最后，我认为他必须解决恐惧的问题，归根结底，国家对手，俄罗斯、中国，

sentences.en: Is he going to find a way to build those much better defenses?
sentences.zh: 以及其他利用网络空间的大国，必须感到恐惧，因为使用这种廉价、有效、隐形的武器所付出的代价根本不值得。

sentences.en: And then finally, I think he's going to have to address the fear question, which is at the end of the day, the state adversaries, Russia, China,
sentences.zh: 而我们还没有找到让他们畏惧我们的正确方法。

sentences.en: the other big nation states that are using cyber, have to fear that the price of making use of this cheap, effective, invisible weapon simply isn't worth it.
sentences.zh: 好的，大卫，非常感谢你。

sentences.en: And we haven't found the right way yet to make them fear us.
sentences.zh: 我们很感激。

sentences.en: Well, David, thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，迈克尔。

sentences.en: We appreciate it.
sentences.zh: 俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京周二发表声明，祝贺拜登当选总统，

sentences.en: Thank you, Michael.
sentences.zh: 并表示期待美俄之间开启合作的新时代。

sentences.en: In a statement on Tuesday, Russian President Vladimir Putin congratulated President-elect Biden on his victory
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: and said he looked forward to a new era of cooperation between the United States and Russia.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还需要了解的其他新闻。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 《泰晤士报》报道称，美国食品药品监督管理局打算在明天某个时候授权使用第二种新冠疫苗，即莫德纳公司生产的疫苗。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 如果获得批准，疫苗剂量最早可能在周一送达美国民众手中。

sentences.en: The Times reports that the FDA intends to authorize use of a second vaccine for the coronavirus, this one made by Moderna, sometime tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 像辉瑞疫苗一样，莫德纳疫苗在大型临床试验中显示出超过90%的有效性。

sentences.en: If approved, doses of it could begin reaching Americans by Monday.
sentences.zh: 而且

sentences.en: Like the Pfizer vaccine, Moderna's has been shown in large clinical trials to be more than 90% effective.
sentences.zh: 我们中有数百万人曾希望总统选举能产生不同的结果。

sentences.en: And
sentences.zh: 但我们的政府体制有既定的程序来决定谁将在1月20日宣誓就职。

sentences.en: Many millions of us had hoped the presidential election would yield a different result.
sentences.zh: 选举人团已经发声了。

sentences.en: But our system of government has processes to determine who will be sworn in on January the 20th.
sentences.zh: 在数周拒绝承认乔·拜登在选举中获胜后，国会中最有权势的共和党人，

sentences.en: The Electoral College has spoken.
sentences.zh: 肯塔基州参议员、参议院多数党领袖米奇·麦康奈尔，终于在周二于参议院发表讲话时承认了这一点。

sentences.en: After weeks of refusing to recognize Joe Biden's victory in the election, the most powerful Republican in Congress,
sentences.zh: 在拒绝承认乔·拜登赢得大选数周后，国会中最有权势的共和党人，

sentences.en: Senate Majority Leader Mitch McConnell of Kentucky, finally did so on Tuesday in a speech from the Senate floor.
sentences.zh: 来自肯塔基州的参议院多数党领袖米奇·麦康奈尔，终于在周二的参议院会议厅演讲中承认了这一结果。

sentences.en: So today I want to congratulate President-elect Joe Biden.
sentences.zh: 今天，我要向当选总统乔·拜登表示祝贺。

sentences.en: The President-elect is no stranger to the Senate.
sentences.zh: 这位当选总统对参议院并不陌生。

sentences.en: He's devoted himself to public service for many years.
sentences.zh: 多年来，他一直致力于公共服务事业。

sentences.en: I also want to congratulate the Vice President-elect, our colleague from California, Senator Harris.
sentences.zh: 我也要向当选副总统、我们来自加利福尼亚州的同事哈里斯参议员表示祝贺。

sentences.en: Given McConnell's stature, his acceptance of Biden's win is a strong signal to the rest of his Republican colleagues in Congress
sentences.zh: 鉴于麦康奈尔的地位，他承认拜登胜选向国会其余共和党同僚发出了一个强有力的信号，

sentences.en: that resistance is now futile and that it's time to turn the page on the Trump era.
sentences.zh: 即抵抗已无意义，现在是时候翻开特朗普时代这一页了。

sentences.en: Today's episode was produced by Jessica Chung and Alexandra Lee Young.
sentences.zh: 今天的节目由杰西卡·钟和亚历山德拉·李·杨制作。

sentences.en: It was edited by Paige Cowan and M.J.
sentences.zh: 由佩奇·考恩和M.J.编辑，

sentences.en: Davis-Lynn and engineered by Chris Wood.
sentences.zh: 戴维斯-林恩负责剪辑，克里斯·伍德担任音频工程。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 以上就是本期《每日新闻》的全部内容。

sentences.en: I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: See you tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 明天见。

sentences.en: This week on The Wirecutter Show, we're getting ready for hosting over the holidays.
sentences.zh: 本周的《Wirecutter秀》节目，我们将为您准备假日待客之道。

sentences.en: Tune in for tips on making your guests feel at home.
sentences.zh: 敬请收听，获取让客人们宾至如归的小贴士。

sentences.en: Are they a blackout sleeper?
sentences.zh: 他们是需要全黑环境才能入睡的人吗？

sentences.en: I don't mean do they black out to go to sleep.
sentences.zh: 我指的不是那种喝到断片才睡觉的人。

sentences.en: I mean, what kind of light do they require?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们对光线有什么要求？

sentences.en: Because that is a very specific thing.
sentences.zh: 因为这可是非常具体的问题。

sentences.en: Do they have allergies, food sensitivities?
sentences.zh: 他们有过敏症或食物敏感吗？

sentences.en: Are they coffee tea drinkers?
sentences.zh: 他们喜欢喝咖啡还是茶？

sentences.en: What time do they like to get up?
sentences.zh: 他们喜欢几点起床？

sentences.en: Find The Wirecutter Show on the New York Times app or wherever you like to listen.
sentences.zh: 您可以在《纽约时报》应用程序或您喜欢的任何播客平台收听《Wirecutter秀》。
